chunks: What the snares seize, and they cut off something from it, then that is dead (carrion). And what you reach of the rest of its body, then slaughter it ritually, then eat from it.

key_terms.الْحَبَائِلُ: Snares/traps used for hunting animals, as opposed to hunting dogs or arrows
key_terms.فَذَكِّهِ: From tadhkiya (تذكية) - the proper Islamic ritual slaughter that makes an animal's meat halal
key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: Dead flesh/carrion (maytah) - meat that has not been ritually slaughtered and is therefore haram

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating meat from an animal caught by a snare or trap?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) provides a jurisprudential ruling on hunting with snares or traps. If the snare cuts off a limb or part of the animal, that severed part is considered dead (maytah) and is forbidden to consume. However, if the hunter reaches the animal while it is still alive (i.e., the rest of its body is still living), he must perform a proper ritual slaughter (tadhkiya) and then it becomes permissible to eat. This ruling reflects the principle that proper ritual slaughter is the only way to make an animal lawful to consume.
